Homecoming limo & party bus transportation in Scottsdale & Phoenix

Scottsdale Sprinters is a Scottsdale chauffeured transportation company serving metro Phoenix. Homecoming night is four logistics problems in formalwear: collecting the group from several houses, getting to the photo spot, arriving at the dance together, and getting everyone home at the hour the parents were told. One chauffeured vehicle, one written schedule and a guardian contact on the reservation covers all four.

How homecoming transportation works here

A homecoming booking is a chauffeured hourly charter that covers the whole evening: pickups at each house (or one staging address the group meets at), an optional dinner or photo stop, the drop at the dance, and returns inside the hours you reserved. Stops on an hourly charter are complimentary — you already bought the time. Send the passenger count, every pickup address in the order you want them run, and a guardian cell when you book; the chauffeur then works one written schedule instead of a group chat.

What it costs (before tax)

We publish hourly rates from $145 to $325 for the vehicles on this page, with a 4-hour minimum on every vehicle listed here except the 56-Passenger Motorcoach (5 hours). A 5-hour homecoming night in the Pink Hummer Limo (18) is $1,475 before tax; the Party Bus (28 Pax) is $1,250; the Limo Lounge Party Sprinter is $875. Arizona sales tax of 8% is added at checkout, and on a card a 50% deposit holds the date. The fare belongs to the vehicle, so one more friend joining does not change it.

Which vehicle for your homecoming group

Count everyone who has to ride together before you look at rates. The Pink Hummer Limo seats 18 and is the arrival the curb photos are built around. The party cabins bring lounge seating, sound and lights, and seat 13–28 passengers per vehicle: the Party Bus (28 Pax), Limo Lounge Party Sprinter, Limo Party Sprinter (13 Pax) and Ultra Luxury Party Sprinter. If parents want their own arrival, or the group is bigger than one cabin, the shuttles and coaches seat 14–56 passengers per vehicle: the Executive Black Sprinter, Executive White Sprinter, Mini Bus (24 Pax), Grech Executive Mini Coach (27 Pax), Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) and 56-Passenger Motorcoach. If the group does not fit one cabin, a second vehicle can be quoted on the same written itinerary — send the full headcount and the stop list with your request so the schedule is built from it.

A sample homecoming night timeline

Every school sets its own start time, so treat this as a shape rather than a schedule. The order is what repeats: load the group without chaos, leave room for photos or dinner, arrive at the dance together, and get everyone home on a plan the parents have already read. The times further down are illustrative only.

Staggered home pickups, or one staging house

There are two ways to start the night and one of them is slower. A stop list of homes means the chauffeur works curb by curb, and every extra driveway is minutes — so the first pickup goes earlier than people expect. One staging house, where the group meets and leaves together, buys that time back. Either works; confirm the addresses and their order when you book so the schedule is built around the real route.

Dinner or a photo stop before the dance

Optional, and it fits inside the hours you already reserved. Restaurant, park, a desert backdrop or a neighborhood photo house — tell us the address when you book so the chauffeur can plan curb access instead of circling the block with the group inside. Confetti and food stay outside the cabin (ride rules).

Dance arrival

The whole point of a dedicated vehicle is that everybody gets out at the same moment, in front of the same doors, instead of trickling in from four different cars. We time the drop to the dance start rather than “sometime around then,” and the return pickup point is part of the written schedule, not something anyone has to negotiate by text at the end of the night.

Returns inside the reserved hours

Within the hours you booked, students go back to the homes or the staging address on the schedule. If the night runs long, extend before the clock runs out — same published hourly rate, subject to availability. Any after-homecoming stop goes on the request too: timing, venue access and the return plan are reviewed before the route is confirmed.

Example 5-hour block (illustrative only — not a published schedule): 4:45 p.m. first pickup → 5:30 p.m. last pickup → 6:15 p.m. photo stop → 7:30 p.m. dance arrival → returns as booked. Slide the whole block to your school’s start time; the order is what holds.

Parent peace-of-mind: one chauffeur, one schedule, one contact

The chauffeur assigned to the night is licensed and insured, and the cabin is detailed between every trip — not at the end of the day. Bottled water on every ride.

On board, the house rules are the same ones every other trip runs on — a school dance does not get a looser version. If anyone travelling is under 21, the trip is alcohol-free for the whole group, adults included:

Put a guardian cell number on the reservation. It gives the chauffeur one point of contact for the evening — a pickup that shifts, a dance that lets out early, a change to the return — instead of a parent and a student trying to reach each other mid-night. Same practice we recommend for prom night. Playlist and lights are welcome.

  • No underage drinking. Anyone under 21 stays on soft drinks.
  • No eating or food inside the vehicle. Drinks are fine; snacks wait for the next stop.
  • No smoking or vaping of any kind. The smell does not leave, so this one carries a fee. $1,500.
  • Keep the drinks in the cups. Minor spills are fine; a can or two on the floor counts as excessive and carries a cleaning fee. $450.
  • If someone gets sick in the vehicle, we have to deep clean it, and that carries a cleaning fee. Pace yourselves. $450.
  • No heels or shoes on the seats. They are leather and they remember.
  • Take your trash with you at the end. Cans, cups, confetti, all of it.

How to book and how far ahead

  1. Count everyone who has to ride together, then pick the vehicle that holds them
  2. Set the date, the first pickup time and the stop list (homes or one staging address, photos or dinner, the dance, returns)
  3. Confirm online — or call/text (623) 986-6339 / email reservations@scottsdalesprinters.com
  4. Pay the deposit — on a card that is 50% — to hold the date

How far ahead: Availability varies by date and by vehicle. Request a current quote for your date and we confirm in writing what is open. A homecoming date is an event date: once the school publishes it and you have a rough headcount, hold the vehicle.

Have ready when you book: the dance date, passenger count, every pickup address (or the staging house), any photo or dinner stop, the dance venue address, your first pickup time, the return plan, and a guardian cell number.

Live availability and checkout sit on the pricing page. If you would rather sanity-check the schedule with a person first, contact reservations or read the FAQ.

Frequently asked questions

Is alcohol allowed if anyone in the group is under 21?

No. If even one passenger is under 21, the trip is alcohol-free for the whole group, adults included — that is our house rule, not a homecoming rule. Tell reservations the passenger ages and the guardian contact when you arrange the written schedule, and it is recorded before pickup. Bottled water on every ride. Full rules: ride rules.

How do parents stay in the loop during the night?

Put a guardian cell number on the reservation. That gives the chauffeur one point of contact if timing shifts — a pickup running late, a dance letting out early, a change to the return — so nobody is chasing a student’s phone mid-evening. The stop list and return plan are confirmed in writing before the night, which is the other half of the answer.

Can we do several home pickups, a photo stop and the dance on one booking?

Yes — that is the standard homecoming shape. On an hourly charter the stops are complimentary because the time is already reserved. Send every address in the order you want them run, and the whole evening goes on one written schedule.

What about after-homecoming events?

Add the stop and the guardian contact to the request. Timing, venue access and the return plan are reviewed before the route is confirmed in writing, so you have the answer before you pay rather than at the curb.

Can the group play its own music — is there Bluetooth?

It depends which vehicle you book. Sound and lighting are what the party cabins are built for — the Party Bus (28 Pax) and the limo Sprinters; the executive Sprinters are the quieter option. Each fleet page lists what that vehicle actually carries, and reservations will confirm before you pay.

What holds the date, and what happens if plans change?

How the rest settles depends on how you pay: on a card, a 50% deposit holds the date and your written confirmation sets out the balance and its timing; paying in full at checkout leaves nothing else due before your ride; a payment link from the reservations desk opens that same checkout. A standard booking refunds in full 14 or more days before pickup; between 72 hours and 14 days the deposit is kept; inside 72 hours the reservation is non-refundable. A group that books 20+ passengers or 2 or more vehicles — a whole friend group plus a parent shuttle, say — falls under the large-group window instead: full refund 30+ days out. Complete terms, including major-event dates: policies.

How is homecoming different from prom night?

Operationally it is the same booking: same fleet, same hourly charter, same house rules, same guardian contact on the reservation. The difference is the calendar — homecoming is the fall dance, prom night is the spring one. The other milestone families plan the same way is a quinceañera transportation day.

Which Valley cities do you cover for homecoming?

We run across Scottsdale, Phoenix and the East Valley. The cities with their own coverage page are Scottsdale, Phoenix, Paradise Valley, Tempe, Mesa, Chandler, Gilbert, Glendale, Cave Creek and San Tan Valley. Confirm every address when you book so drive time sits inside your reserved hours rather than eating the dance.
